LESSON: SAFETY IN THE IMMEDIATE ENVIRONMENT

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: PRE-TECHNICAL STUDIES
Strand: Foundations of Pre-Technical Studies
Topic 1.2: Safety in the Immediate Environment
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 6

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Safety in the Immediate Environment, part of Foundations of Pre-Technical Studies in Grade 7 PRE-TECHNICAL STUDIES.

Key inquiry question: how to protect self and others from 1. Why is safety in the immediate environment important? 2. How can online threats be safeguarded against?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. brainstorm with peers on potential safety threats in the immediate environment (physical and online),

2. use print or digital media to search for information on potential hazards to personal safety in the immediate environment (falls, common road crashes, slips, trips, fires)

3. use print or digital media to search for information on physical threats to digital devices (theft, natural disasters, hardware failure) and online threats in the immediate environment and list them (cyberbullying, impersonation, phishing, hacking, friend requests from unknown people),

4. share ideas and practice on

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. brainstorm with peers on potential safety threats in the immediate environment (physical and online),
2. use print or digital media to search for information on potential hazards to personal safety in the immediate environment (falls, common road crashes, slips, trips, fires)
3. use print or digital media to search for information on physical threats to digital devices (theft, natural disasters, hardware failure) and online threats in the immediate environment and list them (cyberbullying, impersonation, phishing, hacking, friend requests from unknown people),
4. share ideas and practice on

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Safety in the Immediate Environment together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Learning to Learn: learner develops skills of sharing learnt knowledge when taking turns with peers to share ideas on safety

for self and others in the immediate environment.

• Digital Literacy: learner develops skills of interacting with technology when searching for information on potential hazards

to personal safety in the immediate environment.

Values:
• Respect: learner appreciates diverse opinions when sharing information with peers on the online threats.

• Responsibility: learner engages in assigned roles when role playing on safety for self and others in the immediate

environment.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

• Disaster Risk Reduction: learner observes safety when role playing on safety of self and others in the immediate

environment.

• Safety and Security: safety awareness on threats such as falls, road crashes, slips, trips, and fires is enhanced when sharing

ideas and practices on how to protect self and others from threats in the immediate environment.

Link to other Subjects:

Integrated Science when the learner observes safety when working in a science laboratory.
